hints: Notice the reagent is hot ethanolic NaOH, so think elimination to form alkenes rather than substitution to form an alcohol.
Draw out $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and see that H can be removed from C1 to give pent-1-ene or from C3 to give pent-2-ene.
Check each C=C for cis-trans isomerism by asking if each double-bond carbon has two different groups, then count each stereoisomer as a separate hydrocarbon.
walkthrough:
**Recognise elimination to alkenes**

Hot ethanolic NaOH acts as a base and removes HBr from the bromoalkane. This is dehydrohalogenation.

General rule:
$$\text{bromoalkane} + \text{NaOH (ethanolic, heat)} \rightarrow \text{alkene} + \text{NaBr} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the structural isomers**

For 2-bromopentane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, the Br is on C2. H can be lost from two different neighbours.

From C1: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, pent-1-ene.

From C3: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, pent-2-ene.

**Add stereoisomerism**

Pent-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-$. One carbon of the C=C has two H atoms, so no E/Z isomerism is possible.

Pent-2-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Each C of the C=C has two different groups, so both E (trans) and Z (cis) forms exist.

**Count the hydrocarbons**

We have 1 form of pent-1-ene plus 2 stereoisomers of pent-2-ene. That gives 1 + 2 = 3 different hydrocarbon products.

options.A: Not correct. This assumes only one elimination product, ignoring that H can be removed from either side of C2 to give both pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene.
options.B: Not correct. This counts the two structural isomers, pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene, but forgets stereoisomerism. Pent-2-ene exists as E and Z forms which must be counted separately.
options.C: Correct. Elimination gives pent-1-ene (1 form, no stereoisomers) and pent-2-ene (2 forms, E and Z). Total is 3 different hydrocarbons.
options.D: Not correct. This overcounts, perhaps by thinking pent-1-ene also has stereoisomers. Only pent-2-ene has two different groups on each C=C carbon, so only it shows E/Z isomerism.
